comments.body:
AC1 design decision, with the measurement that settled it.

Both branches AC1 permits were investigated. Took branch (a) — the case declares acceptability — and rejected branch (b), scoring a later pipeline stage.

Why Pass 1 cannot carry the distinction, measured rather than assumed: the union of keys on real Pass-1 findings captured in the e508 diagnostic run is {checklist_item, criteria, evidence, finding, impact, location, scenarios, suggested_fix}. `impact` looked like a severity candidate, so I read its value on the captured finding: it is an empty free-text string, not a graded axis. That matches the rubric's own contract (code-review-tests.md:6 "No model-emitted severity (computed deterministically in Pass 3)" and :142 "Do NOT emit severity/confidence/priority").

Why branch (b) was rejected: `pass3_decide` (decide.py:585) returns INDETERMINATE without a `verification` block, so reaching the stage where severity exists requires running Pass 2 — another LLM call per case. `impact_code` (decide.py:545) consumes the verifier's consequence binaries (silent_failure, escapes_automation, trigger_likelihood, prod_impact, churn90, ...), none of which exist on a Pass-1 finding. Beyond the cost, it makes the eval a weaker oracle for the thing it exists to calibrate: a Pass-1 finder regression would be hidden whenever Pass 2 or 3 happened to drop the finding.

Implementation: new `ADVISORY_EXPECTS = frozenset({"advisory"})` in eval_scorers.py, folded into ALLOWED_EXPECTS. `_no_fire` stands down on it (documented in its docstring); eval.py already routes any non-fire/no-fire expect into the "run it, don't score it in the calibration view" path, so the case still executes live and its output is still held to the grounding scorers. It is not a vacuous pass.

The new expectation has a real user rather than being dead vocabulary: FP-preexisting-code-gap-no-new-behaviour. That case's own note already said "guard (vii) keeps that advisory" while its `expect: pass` demanded the opposite — the fixture was internally contradictory. It is now `expect: advisory`, and the note says why.

Guard (vii) is unchanged, per AC1's last sentence. FP-deliberate-tightening passes by having its own second defect fixed instead: it tested only the rejection path, so the reviewer had a genuine coverage gap to flag. Added the happy-path assertion. Guard (vii) now never engages there.

AC2: the loc-ceiling mirror diff now imports SRC_ROOT/gate_file_loc/read_limit and defines line_counts (it previously referenced an undefined name and would have raised NameError).
AC3: the rule-5 glob loop now materializes the glob and asserts non-emptiness, so it cannot pass vacuously.
AC4: the pre-existing-code diff no longer adds a new public `format_release_tag`; it adds only a docstring to a two-year-old function, so it introduces no new observable behaviour and no longer contradicts its own note.
AC6 verified: epochs 3, gate at_least(2), coverage_threshold 0.8, model unchanged; 33 cases before and after, no `- id:` line added or removed.

`make lint` exits 0, including the complexity, mechanism-delta and module-size ratchets. Offline suite: tests/unit/test_code_review_evals.py + test_new_eval_specs.py + test_plan_review_novelty.py, 49 passed.

AC5 (full live 3-epoch eval, local gate_source, AWS_PROFILE=frontier) is running now. AC7 `make verify` follows.

comments.body:
AC5 first live run: `passed=false`, but the picture improved and the remaining failures are informative.

Baseline on origin/main had 6 distinct failing cases. After AC1–AC4 it is 3, and all three are `FP-loc-*`: FP-loc-ceiling-single-sourced-mirror (2/3), FP-loc-numeric-budget-not-a-file-size (2/3), FP-loc-anti-fragmentation-floor (1/3). coverage 1.0, elapsed 1643s. Every fixture the ACs name now passes.

I assumed the loc family was the reviewer over-generalizing the loc-ceiling antipattern to any `<= N` bound, and that assumption was wrong. Capturing the actual Pass-1 findings for those three cases showed the reviewer is correct in each, and firing under different guards than loc-ceiling-pinning:

- FP-loc-anti-fragmentation-floor references `line_counts`, which is undefined in test_get_rotation.py. The reviewer searched the file, reported `(no matches)`, and noted the assertion would raise NameError. That is AC2's defect class exactly, in a case AC2 does not name.
- FP-loc-numeric-budget-not-a-file-size asserts only `len(base) + len(out) <= 500`, which passes as `0 <= 500` on an empty prefetch. That is AC3's defect class exactly, in a case AC3 does not name.

So the ticket's Cause B — defective fixtures — is real in 6 cases, not the 4 the ACs enumerate. The two extras are the same two defect classes already named, so this is an enumeration gap in the ACs rather than new work, and AC5 cannot report passed=true while they stand. Fixed both in place; no case added or removed, header untouched.

Two further corrections the reviewer earned, worth recording because both were my errors, not its:

1. My AC2 fix invented an API. I wrote `from rebar.module_size_support import ...` and called `gate_file_loc(p)` per path. The reviewer checked the real helper and reported that `gate_file_loc()` is zero-arg and already returns the whole `{path: loc}` mapping, that the module lives at `tests/module_size_support.py` and is imported as `from module_size_support import ...`, and that no `src/rebar/module_size_support.py` exists. I verified all three against the tree — it was right on every point. The fixture now uses `gate_file_loc()` zero-arg with the existing import block.
2. An intermediate version asserted `all(count <= limit for ...)`, and the reviewer flagged that it discards which module violated, citing the sibling `test_no_src_module_over_the_hard_cap` that reports the offending set. Also correct; the fixture now builds an `over` dict and asserts it is empty with the violators in the message.

Targeted re-check of just those three cases against the live model: 0 findings each. Full 3-epoch eval re-running now for AC5.

comments.body:
AC5 second live run and the root-cause measurement. `passed=false`, `epoch_pass [false,true,false]`, coverage 1.0, elapsed 1728s. One clean epoch, which had never happened in any prior run.

AC1–AC4 and AC6 are met. The two extra Cause-B fixtures from the last comment are fixed and both passed every epoch of this run. What remains is a third cause the ticket does not identify, and it is not fixture-attributable.

**The failures are nondeterministic, and the evidence is direct.** No case failed all 3 epochs in either run. The failing sets are nearly disjoint between runs on near-identical fixture content:

| Run | distinct failing no-fire cases |
|---|---|
| eval1 | loc-ceiling-mirror (2/3), loc-numeric-budget (2/3), loc-anti-fragmentation (1/3) |
| eval2 | deliberate-tightening (2/3), failopen-drives-real-send-path (1/3), failopen-grep-with-liveness-sentinel (1/3), loc-anti-fragmentation (1/3), rule5-structural-grep (1/3) |

`deliberate-tightening` and `rule5-structural-grep` had identical content in both runs: clean 3/3 in eval1, failing in eval2. The two `failopen-*` cases were never touched by this ticket and fired for the first time in eval2.

I then re-ran the exact 5 cases that failed eval2, 3 reps each, against the live model: **0 findings in all 15**. Pooled with the earlier 3-case re-run, 18 consecutive clean runs on cases the full eval had just failed.

Before trusting that, I checked that the diagnostic reproduces the eval's execution path, because a probe that cannot detect the thing it is pointed at returns a confident wrong answer. `run_eval` dispatches through `_live_solver` (eval.py:663), which calls `run_case` WITHOUT `repo_root`, whereas my harness used `_criterion_solver` (eval.py:519), which passes it. That looked like a material difference. It is not: `run_case` (eval_solver.py:344-350) falls back to `_config.repo_root()`, and I measured that it resolves to the same worktree path both bare and inside the gate session. Same path, same repo_root.

**The nondeterminism is irreducible by configuration.** The spec pins `model: anthropic:claude-opus-4-8`. `capabilities.py:233` records `supports_temperature: False` for it, and `runner.py:498-511` withdraws the parameter rather than sending it — the model rejects a pinned temperature, so the eval cannot be made deterministic that way. No seed is plumbed into the op's request either: `seed` exists only for LLM-judge grader scorers (eval.py:150) and for plan_replay sampling, not for the reviewer under test.

**Arithmetic, on 16 no-fire cases (measured from both junit files, not assumed).** eval1 5 false fires / 48 case-epochs; eval2 6 / 48; pooled 11/96 = 11.5%. An epoch passes only if all 16 no-fire cases pass, so P(clean epoch) = 0.885^16 ≈ 0.14 and `at_least(2)` of 3 ≈ 5%. Using the rate pooled with the 18 clean diagnostic runs (6/66 = 9.1%) it is ≈12%. So the gate passes somewhere between 1 run in 8 and 1 in 20, at ~29 minutes and ~99 model calls per run.

The fixture work did move the number: the ticket's baseline was ~3.3 false fires per epoch (≈20.6% per case), and it is now ~11.5%. But the last round of fixture repair did not reduce it further — it only changed which cases fire. Roughly 7 of the 16 no-fire cases have fired at least once; it is a corpus-wide property of the Pass-1 reviewer, not a defect in any particular fixture.

**AC5 as written is therefore not reachable by the work this ticket scopes.** It is reachable by re-running until a lucky run, which is precisely the retry-until-green behaviour AGENTS.md forbids, and it would leave the actual defect in place. The real remaining defect is the reviewer prompt's baseline false-fire rate on no-fire cases; reducing it means calibrating the FP guards in `code-review-tests.md` and re-measuring recall on the 16 fire cases, which is outside this ticket's stated Scope ("In scope: `_no_fire`'s severity blindness, and the four named fixtures").

Not proposing to loosen the gate: Scope rules it out and AC6 freezes `epochs`/`gate`/`coverage_threshold`. Escalating to the user for the disposition rather than choosing one.

compiled_state.description:
## Problem

The `code-review-tests` eval spec's gate cannot pass, and has not been able to for some time. Measured on `origin/main` b7c6ed6c834 with the full 3-epoch run and no case cap:

| Run | Cases | Distinct failing | coverage | epoch_pass |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `origin/main`, unmodified | 33 | 6 | 1.0 | `[false,false,false]` |
| With story e508's 6 added cases | 39 | 5 | 1.0 | `[false,false,false]` |

No clean epoch in 6 measured (baseline 3/4/3 failing, e508 4/3/3). `_gating_results` passes an epoch only when every applicable case passes, so with roughly 3.3 false-fires per epoch over 20 no-fire cases the `at_least(2)` of 3 gate is unreachable.

Every failure in both runs is a pre-existing no-fire ("FP") case. None of e508's 6 added cases failed in any epoch.

This went unseen because CI never actually scored the spec — bug `77b6-868f-f4bd-461f` (`dissocial-unpleasant-adouri`): the `eval-live` job calls `run_eval` outside a gate session, so every case errors unscored, and `continue-on-error: true` hides it.

## Root cause

Two distinct causes, both confirmed by re-running the four recurring FP cases through `eval_solver.run_case` and reading the raw findings (4 cases x 3 reps; 8 of 12 runs fired). They are not random miscalibration — every captured finding is well-evidenced and correct.

**Cause A — the scorer cannot see the advisory/blocking distinction the rubric relies on.**

`eval_solver.run_case` returns raw Pass-1 findings. Pass-1 findings carry no severity: advisory-vs-blocking is assigned downstream in `code_review/finalize.py`, from the Pass-2 verdict and the routed thresholds. `_no_fire` (`eval_scorers.py:229-234`) fails on ANY non-empty findings list.

Several of the rubric's FP guards are written to DOWNGRADE a finding to advisory, not to suppress it. Guard (vii) is explicitly of this shape. A case whose correct behaviour is "emit an advisory finding" therefore cannot pass `_no_fire` by construction.

This is directly observable. On `FP-deliberate-tightening` the reviewer emitted a finding whose own evidence reads: "this coverage gap is advisory rather than blocking per guard (vii)". The reviewer applied the guard exactly as written, and the scorer failed it anyway.

**Cause B — four FP fixtures each carry a second, unrelated, real defect.**

Each fixture isolates one antipattern and asserts "must NOT fire". But the synthetic diff in each also exhibits a genuine separate problem, so a correct reviewer fires on the second one:

- `FP-loc-ceiling-single-sourced-mirror` — the added assertion iterates `line_counts`, which the fixture never defines or imports. The test as written would raise `NameError`. The reviewer reports exactly that.
- `FP-rule5-structural-grep` — the added test is a bare `for md in reviewers_dir.glob(...)` with no non-emptiness guard, so it passes vacuously on an empty glob. That is a real vacuous-test defect, distinct from the source-grep antipattern under test.
- `FP-deliberate-tightening` — only the rejection path is tested; no happy-path assertion, so an inverted guard would ship undetected. (Also hits cause A.)
- `FP-preexisting-code-gap-no-new-behaviour` — the note says the untested branch is reachable only through pre-existing lines, but the diff ADDS a new public `format_release_tag` with new observable behaviour and no test. The fixture contradicts its own premise.

## Scope

In scope: `_no_fire`'s severity blindness, and the four named fixtures. Out of scope: the CI invocation defect (bug `77b6`), and any change to epoch/gate semantics — making the gate pass by loosening `at_least(2)` or the all-cases-must-pass rule would hide the defect rather than fix it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1 — A no-fire case can express that an advisory finding is acceptable. `_no_fire` distinguishes a finding the rubric downgrades from one it surfaces as blocking, or the eval scores a stage at which that distinction exists. `FP-deliberate-tightening` passes without its guard-(vii) behaviour changing.
- [ ] AC2 — `FP-loc-ceiling-single-sourced-mirror`'s diff defines or imports every name it references, so the fixture exhibits only the mirror form it is testing.
- [ ] AC3 — `FP-rule5-structural-grep`'s diff carries a non-emptiness guard, so it exhibits only the structural-grep form it is testing.
- [ ] AC4 — `FP-preexisting-code-gap-no-new-behaviour`'s diff adds no new observable behaviour, so it matches its own note.
- [ ] AC5 — A full live `rebar.llm.evals.eval.run_eval("code-review-tests")` (3 epochs, no case cap, inside a `gate_source` local-mode session) reports `passed=true`.
- [ ] AC6 — No change to `epochs`, `gate`, or `coverage_threshold` in `code-review-tests.eval.yaml`, and no case removed from the dataset.
- [ ] AC7 — `make verify` exits 0.

## Evidence paths

Measurement scripts and raw output: `.rebar/scratch/e508-eval/` on branch `impl-e508` — `run.py` (gate-wrapped runner), `baseline.sh` (trapped-restore baseline), `result.json`, `baseline.json`, `diag3.py`/`diag3.log` (raw false-fire capture).

Note for whoever runs the eval: `run_eval` must be wrapped in a `gate_source.gate_read_root` session or every case errors unscored and surfaces only as `coverage=0.0`, and the Bedrock backend needs `AWS_PROFILE=frontier` or every case errors the same silent way.
compiled_state.title: Make code-review-tests FP cases passable: advisory findings and self-defeating fixtures
